requirements.evidence: CreateQueue authorizes via Gate 'create' [Queue::class, $entity], trims/limits name, slugifies default or explicit slug, checks per-entity uniqueness and maps a racing QueryException to ValidationException (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:18-41). UpdateQueue takes nullable named params, excludes its own id from the slug check, locks the queue and handles the race (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:20-69). SetQueueAccess upserts or revokes, rejects unknown or non-string permissions and cross-entity memberships, and logs queue.access.granted/revoked on Log::channel('audit') with actor_id/queue_id/entity_membership_id, and only when a row was deleted (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:43-75). The migration matches the spec (FK cascades, json permissions, unique pair). The policy's call ability handles managers, employee grants and non-array values (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:45-71). CallNextTicket authorizes after the inactive check (CallNextTicket.php:32), and Ticket::call() follows lock -> inactive -> authorize -> LogicException (app/Models/Ticket.php:89-109). The enum, the model and the same-entity factory match the contract. No delete action was added.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through app/Actions with authorization inside each action via QueuePolicy. $fillable is set through #[Fillable] on QueueAccess. The migration has a generated-style timestamp name and a reversible down(). Docs and CHANGELOG are updated. One deviation: the existing 'Single-ticket call (scope note)' paragraph in docs/business-rules.md still says Ticket::call() is 'entity-membership checked' and 'AuthZ stays out of scope', which now contradicts the new section directly above it.

security.evidence: Every new action authorizes before writing: Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize(...) in CreateQueue.php:18, UpdateQueue.php:36 and SetQueueAccess.php:37. Authorization runs against the locked queue row. SetQueueAccess re-fetches the membership and checks the entity match (SetQueueAccess.php:41-47). Both call paths now enforce 'call'. The non-array permissions value fails closed (QueuePolicy.php:68-69). Mass assignment is restricted with #[Fillable], and the actions use forceCreate only with server-built attributes.

tests.evidence: Five new test files cover create, update, set access, the policy and the call paths. They include happy paths, validation failures (blank/long names, unusable slugs, unknown/non-string/nested permissions), unauthorized actors (employee, foreign owner, non-member) with 'nothing written' assertions, an every-mode dataset for CallNextTicket, corrupted JSON grants, audit message/context and channel, a simulated slug race (CreateQueueTest 'turns a unique index violation...'), ordering of the inactive check before authorization, and the already-called ticket case. Existing CallNextTicket tests were adjusted to use owners rather than weakened. Small gaps: no race test for UpdateQueue, and the cascade test only deletes the membership, not the queue.

simplicity.evidence: Code is lean overall. The shared NormalizesQueueFields trait (app/Actions/Concerns/NormalizesQueueFields.php) removes duplication between Create and Update. Validation is hand-rolled with ValidationException::withMessages instead of Laravel's Validator, a small reinvention. The UpdateQueue catch block re-normalizes the slug and copies attributes back via setRawAttributes, which adds some indirection.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are small and PHPDoc explains intent (e.g. the lock-order comment at Ticket.php:90). The race-handling try/catch wrapping the whole transaction in UpdateQueue.php:27-66 and the closure-heavy factory definition (QueueAccessFactory.php:28-32) take a moment to follow. No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: actions, enum, model, factory, migration, policy, call-path enforcement, docs, CHANGELOG and tests. The userWithRole helper in tests/Pest.php supports the new tests. No UI, no deletion action and no unrelated refactors.

issues.location: docs/business-rules.md (existing 'Single-ticket call (scope note)' paragraph after the new section)
issues.explanation: This paragraph still describes Ticket::call() as only entity-membership checked with AuthZ out of scope, which contradicts the new authorization rules added in the same file.
No test covers the path that maps a racing unique-index violation to ValidationException in UpdateQueue (only CreateQueue's race is tested).
The test is named for cascading on queue or membership delete but only deletes the membership.
Name and slug validation is hand-written with ValidationException::withMessages, where Laravel's Validator rules would do the same job.
The membership attribute closure calls create() even when the factory is used with make(), and it looks up the queue again just to read its entity_id.

review.summary: The change adds the queue-management domain slice: CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess actions, QueuePolicy, the queue_access table with its model, factory and enum, and call-ability enforcement in both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call() in the required order. Tests are thorough, including authorization, validation, race and audit cases. It meets the contract and conventions closely; remaining nits are a stale docs paragraph and small test gaps. Confidence is medium because some helpers it relies on (User::membershipFor, the EntityMembership employee() state, the queues unique index) are not shown in the diff.
